anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : The optimizer bases its cost estimates on stale or incomplete metadata, causing systematic misestimation of cardinalities and ultimately poor plan choices.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions and rollback records accumulate faster than background cleanup can reclaim them, inflating table and index size and increasing visibility-check costs.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical devices that store data, temp, or log files become throughput- or latency-bound, so every read or write waits behind saturated queues.

When all three root causes appear together, symptoms overlap and magnify: execution plans chosen from incorrect statistics are forced to scan or join vastly larger on-disk structures bloated by version buildup; these larger scans, in turn, drive far more physical I/O against disks that are already maxed out, pushing latency higher and keeping buffer-pool hit ratios low. Administrators observe wildly inaccurate row-count estimates, sudden plan flips after data-change bursts, soaring table and index sizes, nonstop autovacuum or purge activity, steep growth in I/O wait events, and long-running queries that stall during large sequential reads or log flushes. Cleanup workers and statistics refresh jobs may run continuously but still fall behind because every page read or written is throttled by the saturated storage layer, while critical OLTP transactions suffer from both plan inefficiency and I/O backlog.

Causally, MVCC version bloat first enlarges the physical footprint of hot tables and indexes. This footprint inflation invalidates previously correct statistics and raises the volume of data the optimizer must consider, seeding the Optimizer Statistics Anomaly. Misestimated plans often select full scans or sub-optimal join orders that touch even more pages, amplifying storage traffic. The extra I/O exacerbates the Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly, slowing both foreground queries and the background cleaners that would otherwise shrink the version store and trigger statistics refreshes. The stalled cleaners allow even more bloat to accumulate, which further skews statistics and perpetuates a feedback loop of increasing workload cost and diminishing throughput.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits for additional data from a connection longer than net_read_timeout.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
